The intent of writing

June 25th 2026

After having just experienced the joy of writing in html and discovering the freedom and power that comes with the ability of creating arbitrary web pages in a place you own and control, I feel obliged to explore this medium further. By producing the next "piece". Next blog post.

🌌

As with any medium the potential future interactions with the "piece" are outside of the authors reach at the time of creation.

That "out of reach" is exactly what I am attracted to. Trying to compute the audience reaction I will never be able to see at the moment of creation. Even stand-up comedians get a delayed feedback.

People who have created works that are appealing to me, tend to argue that is is not to be prioritized.

After all Github does vring the ability to review the work before publishing. And that is exactly what I should do after this piece is written. Review and identify if this thing moves me. After all creating 10 clay jugs has a higher probabilty of creating a perfect one than just creating one jug, no matter how hard you try to make it perfect.

That brings me to the intent of this piece. It has none. There is no conceivable pirpose behind this piece. The intent can be to practice. But then again that should not be a concern for amyone else. Unless they are in a similar situation. And than we come back to getting concerned about the effect this will have on the reader.

So either the people who have created masterpieces were simply lucky(which some admitting to not foreseeing the success of their work), and some have anticipated the success. That anticipation could have been nothing more than false positive. Having a prediction coming true does heavily rely on the specificity of the prediction. And predicting your piece would be a success, and then having the piece become one, is a classic survivorship bias. Unless the person is able to predict the success accurately for all their pieces, they are not really predicting, merely guessing.

Having said that, this question, on wheather one can predict the success of their work, is one reason why axcomplished authors use pseudomins for their subsequent works. To check if they can.

And so we come back to the intent of writing. Or intent on the creative act. As with anything, we (humans) want to see the world respond to our actions. To explore.

And this: me tapping glass on a train, just to set the electrostatic charges on my device, and then on some other silicone chip, that I will never see, only for this to be made available to you, in whatever medium you are receiving this, to set the electro static charges in your brain, feels magical.

What can be the second, third and fourth order effects is yet to be discovered(or explored) by me
